For each integer point both coordinate deviations from 1/2 are at least 1/2 and the coefficients are strictly positive, proving interior lattice exclusion. Inside the unit square equality occurs only at the four corners, which the predecessor's P_0 excludes.

At s=0 each facet midpoint is one binary corner and the facet length is sqrt(2). The only lattice point on each facet is its midpoint by the same absolute-deviation equality. Multiplying unit normals by the length gives 2(p−(1/2,1/2)); direct summation gives zero vector, 2I_2 and trace four.

Each contact has positive slack in the other three inequalities. For sufficiently small offset perturbations with normals fixed an increase in any one offset therefore makes its contact an interior lattice point. A genuine inward change removes positive area by the relative interior of its original facet.
The two diagonal lengths are 2/(1+s) and 2/(1−s), so area is 2/(1−s^2). Its difference from 2 is 2s^2/(1−s^2), which gives the derivatives zero and four.
